item.title: Missouri officials warn residents to take earthquake preparedness seriously
item.description: Missouri emergency officials are urging residents to take earthquake preparedness seriously as the state marks Earthquake Awareness Month, with the potential for a major event along the New Madrid Seismic Zone to have catastrophic consequences.

item.title: What's wrong with the St. Louis Blues? Five reasons behind this season's struggles
item.description: Heading into the Olympic break, with roughly two-thirds of their season complete, the St. Louis Blues find themselves in somewhat unfamiliar territory. They have lost eight of their last nine games with 49 points, the second-fewest in the league.

item.title: 5 wanted for shooting at man who exited gas station
item.description: District 3 detectives from the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department (SLMPD) are searching for five men wanted in connection to a shooting at a gas station in South St. Louis last month.

item.title: Uncle Bill's 'weeks away' from reopening, developer says
item.description: For long-time denizens of south St. Louis and those in need of late-night nourishment, the sign outside Uncle Bill’s acted as a calling card. A warm invitation to come inside for a hot plate of pancakes or waffles and steaming cup of coffee at all hours of the day or night.

item.title: Jefferson Co. residents call for safety improvements on Route 30
item.description: The High Ridge Fire Protection District Station 1 was filled with concerned residents on Thursday for a town hall meeting about safety concerns on Route 30 in Jefferson County.

item.title: Vendors left unpaid after Jingle! holiday event bankruptcy
item.description: A highly-promoted holiday festival during Christmas 2024 has left vendors and contractors owed anywhere from hundreds to hundreds of thousands of dollars.

item.title: Belleville man accused of photographing women in Wash. Univ. bathroom
item.description: A Belleville, Illinois, man is accused of photographing more than a dozen women in a library bathroom on Washington University campus.

item.title: Soup thrown, shot fired during argument at Kirkwood sushi restaurant
item.description: A St. Louis woman is charged with multiple felonies for allegedly throwing soup and firing a gun inside a Kirkwood restaurant during an argument with staff, believing they were rude to her and her family when they arrived.

item.title: May tornado survivor home is destroyed by fire during roof repairs
item.description: A St. Louis woman who survived last May's tornado is now picking up the pieces again after her home caught fire during roof repairs.

item.title: Local drug case expands into cartel, terrorism allegations
item.description: What began as a local drug investigation in the St. Louis region has expanded into a sweeping federal case with alleged ties to the Sinaloa cartel in Mexico and accusations of narco-terrorism.
